intent.raw_query: New Zealand South Island, $4000, hiking and bungee jumping, November 2026

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video package.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, a stunning 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek through ancient beech forests, alpine meadows, and past glacial lakes with panoramic views of the Harris Saddle. Can be done as a guided day section or multi-day trek with DOC huts.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of the Hooker Valley, Mueller Glacier, and the Southern Alps. Overnight stays in the DOC Mueller Hut offer unforgettable stargazing in one of the world's darkest sky reserves.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the cruise ships arrive, gliding past Mitre Peak and cascading waterfalls. Combine with a guided walk along the Milford foreshore track through ancient rainforest. A truly immersive way to experience one of the world's most spectacular natural wonders.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk through the town center and lakefront. Sample locally sourced Central Otago pinot noir, artisan cheeses, venison sliders, and Fergburger — the legendary burger institution. Learn about Māori culture and the region's gold rush history from knowledgeable local guides.

trip_options.title: Budget Explorer - New Zealand South Island
trip_options.description: Save money without sacrificing the experience. Perfect for travelers who value authentic local experiences over luxury.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of the Hooker Valley, Mueller Glacier, and the Southern Alps. Overnight stays in the DOC Mueller Hut offer unforgettable stargazing in one of the world's darkest sky reserves.

day_by_day.morning: No activities scheduled — flight arrives at 13:00
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Collect luggage and take the Orbus public bus (Route 1, ~$4 NZD) into Queenstown town centre. Grab a late lunch, then arrange transport to Nevis Valley accommodation (pre-book a shared shuttle or rideshare to save costs). Check in and settle in.
day_by_day.evening: Take a short stroll around Queenstown lakefront along Lake Wakatipu — free and stunning. Visit the Queenstown Night Market on Earnslaw Park (open Sundays, ~$5–15 NZD for street food). Grab dinner from a market stall and enjoy the atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Eat at the airport or on the plane
meals.lunch: Fergbaker bakery in Queenstown town centre — pies and rolls from ~$6 NZD
meals.dinner: Queenstown Night Market street food stalls — budget ~$10–15 NZD for a full meal

day_by_day.notes: Pre-book your shuttle from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley accommodation to avoid expensive last-minute taxis. Confirm check-in time with the property as arrival is afternoon. Pick up a free Queenstown map from the i-SITE visitor centre near the waterfront.

day_by_day.morning: After breakfast, hike the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (Te Tapu-nui) — a free 2–3 hour return hike starting from Belfast Street. Gain 500m elevation for panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu, The Remarkables, and Cecil Peak. Bring water and snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Descend and head to the Queenstown Gardens (free entry). Walk the perimeter trail, relax by the lake, and explore the rose garden and disc golf course (free). Visit the nearby Kiwi Birdlife Park exterior for free bird spotting around the gardens area.
day_by_day.evening: Cook a simple meal back at the accommodation using groceries from Countdown Queenstown (~$10–15 NZD). Plan tomorrow's Nevis Bungy logistics — book online in advance for the best price and confirm shuttle pickup time from Queenstown.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — muesli, toast, or eggs from Countdown (~$5 NZD)
meals.lunch: Pack a homemade sandwich and fruit for the Queenstown Hill hike
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta or stir-fry at accommodation (~$8–10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Hill hike is free and one of the best views in the region. Wear sturdy shoes and apply sunscreen — November sun is strong in New Zealand. Book the Nevis Bungy online at least 24 hours ahead for the best rate (~$275 NZD vs walk-up prices).

day_by_day.morning: The big day — Nevis Bungy Jump! AJ Hackett's Nevis Bungy is New Zealand's highest bungy at 134m. The shuttle departs Queenstown town centre (included in booking). Travel through the dramatic Nevis Valley landscape to the platform. Jump time is usually mid-morning.
day_by_day.afternoon: Return shuttle back to Queenstown by early afternoon. Celebrate your jump with a walk along the Queenstown waterfront. Visit the free TSS Earnslaw viewing area and watch the iconic steamship. Browse the Steamer Wharf area without spending — great photo opportunities.
day_by_day.evening: Treat yourself modestly for dinner — visit the Queenstown Night Market (if Monday/Sunday) or grab a budget meal at Vudu Café or Winnies Pizza for a shared pizza deal. Review your GoPro footage from the bungy jump!

meals.breakfast: Self-catered early breakfast before shuttle pickup — banana, toast, peanut butter
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the shuttle ride; grab a cheap pie from a petrol station bakery on return (~$5 NZD)
meals.dinner: Winnies Queenstown — shared pizza deal ~$15–18 NZD per person, great atmosphere

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy shuttle departs from Queenstown — confirm exact pickup location when booking. Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes. Secure loose items. The experience including shuttle is approximately 3–4 hours total. Photos are available to purchase but are expensive — consider the GoPro rental add-on if you want footage.

day_by_day.morning: Drive or take a bus to Glenorchy (1 hour from Queenstown, ~$15 NZD on Connectabus). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Walkway — a flat, easy 1-hour loop through wetlands and forest with stunning views of the Dart River and Richardson Mountains. Free entry.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue on the Routeburn Track Day Walk — hike to the Routeburn Flats (2–3 hours return, free). This section of the famous Routeburn Track passes through beech forest and opens to spectacular alpine meadows. No booking required for day walks.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown/Nevis Valley by early evening. Self-cater dinner at accommodation. Prep hiking gear and snacks for tomorrow's adventure day.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation — oats with honey and banana
meals.lunch: Pack your own lunch — sandwiches, trail mix, energy bars for the Routeburn walk
meals.dinner: Self-cooked rice and canned beans/lentils with vegetables (~$7–9 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Check Connectabus timetable in advance as Glenorchy services are limited. Alternatively, consider carpooling with other travellers from the hostel. The Routeburn Track day walk requires no Great Walk booking — only overnight huts need reservations. Bring insect repellent for the lagoon area.

day_by_day.morning: Head to Arrowtown (30 min from Queenstown by bus or car). Walk the Arrow River Bridges Trail — a free 3km loop following the historic gold rush-era Arrow River with suspension bridges and old mining relics. Explore Arrowtown's charming historic main street.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Lakes District Museum in Arrowtown (entry ~$10 NZD) to learn about the gold rush history. Then hike the Arrowtown Hill Walk — a short steep climb behind the town for panoramic views over the Wakatipu Basin (~45 minutes return, free).
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown for dinner. Try the famous Fergburger — budget ~$14–18 NZD for a burger. Join the queue (it's worth it!) and eat by the lakefront. Early night to rest legs for upcoming big hikes.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at accommodation
meals.lunch: Arrowtown Bakery — pies and sandwiches from ~$6–8 NZD, a local favourite
meals.dinner: Fergburger, Queenstown — iconic NZ burger experience, budget ~$15–18 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is best explored on a weekday to avoid weekend crowds. The Arrow River Bridges Trail is suitable for all fitness levels. November is late spring in NZ — weather can be changeable so bring a light rain jacket. Buses from Queenstown to Arrowtown run via Orbus Route 8.

day_by_day.morning: Travel day to Wanaka (~1 hour from Queenstown by Intercity bus or car, ~$15–20 NZD). Check into budget accommodation in Wanaka (book a hostel dorm for ~$35–45 NZD per night). Drop bags and head straight to Lake Wanaka waterfront — free walking and swimming.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Mount Iron Track — a 1.5-hour return hike (3.2km) rising 240m above Wanaka township with 360-degree views of the lake, mountains, and Clutha River. Free, well-marked trail starting near the town centre.
day_by_day.evening: Explore Wanaka's compact town centre. Visit the famous 'That Wanaka Tree' on the lakefront for sunset photos (free). Grab dinner at a local café or cook at the hostel.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered before departure from Nevis Valley
meals.lunch: Relishes Café, Wanaka — affordable cabinet food and wraps ~$10–13 NZD
meals.dinner: Kai Whakapai Café & Bar — try the budget pasta or burger options ~$18–22 NZD, or self-cater at hostel for ~$8 NZD

day_by_day.notes: Book Wanaka hostel accommodation well in advance — November is shoulder season and good budget options fill quickly. Intercity buses from Queenstown to Wanaka must be pre-booked online. Mount Iron Track is dog-friendly and a great warm-up hike. The 'That Wanaka Tree' is best photographed at golden hour.

day_by_day.morning: Full day adventure — hike the Rob Roy Glacier Track (20km return, 5–6 hours, free). Drive or join a carpool to the Matukituki Valley (45 min from Wanaka). The track passes through ancient beech forest to a dramatic glacial valley with hanging glaciers, waterfalls, and suspension bridges.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue hiking to the Rob Roy Glacier viewpoint. Have lunch at the glacier viewpoint — one of the most spectacular free hikes in the South Island. Begin the return hike through the valley.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka tired but exhilarated. Soak tired muscles with a warm shower. Self-cater a hearty dinner at the hostel — pasta with protein is ideal for recovery. Early bedtime.

meals.breakfast: Early self-catered breakfast before 8am departure — oats, banana, coffee
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at the glacier viewpoint — sandwiches, cheese, crackers, chocolate, trail mix
meals.dinner: Self-cooked pasta with tuna and vegetables at hostel (~$8–10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Rob Roy Glacier Track requires a car or carpool as there is no public transport to the Matukituki Valley trailhead. Check the Wanaka hostel noticeboard or Facebook travel groups to find carpool partners. Start early (8am) to complete the full track comfortably. Bring 2–3 litres of water, sunscreen, and a warm layer — temperatures drop near the glacier.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery morning in Wanaka. Sleep in, then visit Puzzling World (exterior is free to view; entry ~$20 NZD if interested). Walk along the Wanaka lakefront promenade — completely free and beautiful. Visit the local Sunday market at Pembroke Park (~8am–1pm) for fresh produce and cheap snacks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Diamond Lake and Rocky Mountain Loop (3–4 hours, free). Drive or carpool 20 min from Wanaka to the trailhead. The loop takes you past a stunning turquoise lake and up to Rocky Mountain summit for sweeping views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Wanaka. Visit the Wanaka lakefront at sunset — golden hour is spectacular in November. Grab a cheap takeaway or cook at the hostel. Pack bags for tomorrow's travel to Aoraki/Mount Cook.

meals.breakfast: Wanaka Sunday Market — fresh fruit, pastries, and coffee ~$8–10 NZD
meals.lunch: Pack snacks from the market for the Diamond Lake hike
meals.dinner: New World Supermarket Wanaka — self-cater a big meal to fuel up before Mount Cook (~$10 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Diamond Lake trailhead is at Lake Outlet, ~20km from Wanaka — a car or carpool is needed. The track is well-marked but can be slippery after rain. Check weather forecast the night before. Book transport to Aoraki/Mount Cook for tomorrow — Intercity or a shared shuttle (~$40–60 NZD).

day_by_day.morning: Travel day — depart Wanaka for Aoraki/Mount Cook Village (~3 hours via Intercity bus or shuttle). The drive through the Mackenzie Basin is spectacular — turquoise Lake Pukaki and the Southern Alps come into view. Arrive at Mount Cook Village and check into YHA Mount Cook (~$40–50 NZD dorm).
day_by_day.afternoon: Tackle the Kea Point Track (2 hours return, free) — an accessible walk through alpine scrub to a viewpoint directly facing the Mueller Glacier terminal lake and the Hooker Valley. Excellent acclimatisation walk before tomorrow's big hike.
day_by_day.evening: Attend the free DOC ranger talk at the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre (evenings, check schedule). Learn about Aoraki/Mount Cook's geology and climbing history. Self-cater dinner at YHA — use the well-equipped kitchen.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Wanaka hostel before departure
meals.lunch: Pack sandwiches for the bus journey — there are limited food options en route
meals.dinner: Self-cooked meal at YHA Mount Cook — pasta, sauce, and vegetables (~$10–12 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Mount Cook Village has very limited food options and everything is expensive — stock up on groceries in Twizel (on the bus route) or Wanaka before arriving. The YHA has a good kitchen and is the best budget accommodation in the village. Book YHA well in advance for November. The Kea Point Track is suitable for all fitness levels and a great warm-up.

day_by_day.morning: The highlight of the trip — Mueller Hut Route! Start early (7am) from the White Horse Hill Campground. The track climbs steeply 1,000m over 5.4km to Mueller Hut at 1,800m elevation. The first section involves a long staircase (1,200 steps), then a ridge scramble. Stunning views of Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Mueller Glacier, and surrounding peaks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Reach Mueller Hut by mid-morning/noon (depending on pace). Spend time at the hut enjoying the extraordinary 360-degree alpine views. Have lunch with one of the most dramatic backdrops in New Zealand. Begin descent in the early afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Mount Cook Village by late afternoon — legs will be tired! Shower and rest at YHA. Self-cater a high-calorie recovery dinner. Enjoy the incredible Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve — one of the best stargazing locations in the Southern Hemisphere (free).

meals.breakfast: Very early self-catered breakfast at YHA — oats, eggs, coffee before 7am departure
meals.lunch: Packed lunch at Mueller Hut — energy bars, cheese, crackers, dried fruit, nuts
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hearty meal at YHA — rice, lentils, vegetables, and protein (~$12 NZD)

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut Route is a serious alpine hike — check weather forecast the night before and do not attempt in poor visibility or high winds. Bring: 3L water, warm layers, windproof jacket, gloves, sunscreen, sunglasses, and trekking poles if available. The hut is a DOC serviced hut — day visitors welcome but overnight stays require booking (~$55 NZD). November conditions can include snow above 1,500m. Start early to avoid afternoon cloud buildup.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — sleep in and rest tired muscles. Walk the Hooker Valley Track (3 hours return, free) — a flat, easy walk through the Hooker Valley to three swing bridges and the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with floating icebergs. One of NZ's most iconic and accessible walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre (entry ~$20 NZD) — a museum and planetarium dedicated to the first summiteer of Everest and the history of climbing in the Southern Alps. Afternoon departure by shuttle or bus toward Tekapo (~1.5 hours, ~$25–35 NZD).
day_by_day.evening: Arrive in Lake Tekapo. Check into budget accommodation (hostel or holiday park cabin ~$35–50 NZD). Walk to the Church of the Good Shepherd at sunset — the iconic small stone church with turquoise lake backdrop is free to visit. Stargaze at the lake edge after dark.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at YHA Mount Cook — use up remaining food supplies
meals.lunch: Packed lunch on the Hooker Valley Track
meals.dinner: Tekapo Springs café or Kohan Japanese Restaurant, Tekapo — budget ~$18–22 NZD, or self-cater at hostel

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is flat and suitable for all fitness levels — a perfect recovery day walk. Book shuttle from Mount Cook to Tekapo in advance. Lake Tekapo is in the Aoraki Mackenzie International Dark Sky Reserve — if skies are clear, the stargazing is world-class and completely free from the lakefront.

day_by_day.morning: Hike Mount John Summit Loop (2–3 hours return, free) — a well-marked trail from Lake Tekapo township to the summit of Mount John (1,029m) where the University of Canterbury Observatory sits. Panoramic views of the Mackenzie Basin, Lake Tekapo, and the Southern Alps.
day_by_day.afternoon: Travel from Lake Tekapo back toward Queenstown (~3.5 hours via Intercity bus or shuttle, ~$35–50 NZD). Enjoy the scenic drive through the Mackenzie Basin and past Lake Pukaki. Arrive in Queenstown by late afternoon. Return to Nevis Valley accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown — walk the waterfront one last time. Visit the Queenstown Hill lookout for a night view of the lights reflecting on Lake Wakatipu. Grab a final budget dinner and pack for departure.

meals.breakfast: Self-catered at Tekapo hostel — use remaining supplies
meals.lunch: Pack snacks for the bus journey — there are limited stops en route
meals.dinner: Vudu Café & Larder, Queenstown — affordable cabinet food and meals ~$15–20 NZD, or self-cater at accommodation

day_by_day.notes: The Mount John hike starts from the town centre — no transport needed. The observatory café at the summit sells coffee but is expensive (~$7 NZD). Confirm your return bus or shuttle from Tekapo to Queenstown the night before. Check out of Tekapo accommodation by 10am. Reconfirm your outbound flight details for Day 13.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning — wake up early for one last sunrise walk near Nevis Valley or the Queenstown lakefront. Pack all belongings and check out of accommodation. Head into Queenstown for a farewell breakfast at a local café.
day_by_day.afternoon: Depending on departure flight time — if afternoon flight, spend remaining time at the Queenstown Botanic Gardens (free) or browse the Queenstown Arts and Crafts Market. Take the Orbus bus to Queenstown Airport (~$4 NZD). Check in and depart.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Reflect on 13 incredible days of hiking, bungy jumping, glaciers, and South Island adventure!

meals.breakfast: The Waffles on Wharf, Queenstown — budget waffles and coffee ~$12–15 NZD as a farewell treat
meals.lunch: Airport café or pack remaining snacks from accommodation
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at connecting airport

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in — the airport can be busy with international connections. Return any rental gear, settle any outstanding accommodation bills, and ensure you have NZD for the Orbus bus to the airport. Keep receipts for any travel insurance claims. New Zealand has strict biosecurity — dispose of all fresh food before passing through airport biosecurity.

trip_options.title: Classic New Zealand South Island Experience
trip_options.description: The sweet spot between comfort and value. Enjoy quality accommodations, diverse experiences, and good food.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival — Flight LH lands at 13:00, so no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for the trip.
day_by_day.afternoon: Land at Queenstown Airport at 13:00. Clear customs, collect luggage, and transfer to Nevis Valley, Queenstown Boutique Stay (~45 min drive). Check in, freshen up, and take a leisurely orientation walk around the Queenstown lakefront and town center to get your bearings.
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along Lake Wakatipu waterfront at golden hour. Explore the lively Queenstown town center and browse local shops on Beach Street.

meals.breakfast: On the flight or at the airport upon arrival.
meals.lunch: Grab a quick bite at Queenstown Airport — try Vudu Café for a sandwich and coffee.
meals.dinner: Fergburger (iconic Queenstown institution) — expect a short queue but excellent value. Try the 'Ferg' classic beef burger. ~NZD 15–20.

day_by_day.notes: Keep Day 1 light. Focus on acclimatizing to New Zealand time (NZDT, UTC+13). Confirm all activity bookings for the coming days. Pack hiking gear for the week ahead. Queenstown can be breezy in November — bring a light layer.

day_by_day.morning: Explore Queenstown's Skyline Gondola — ride up to Bob's Peak (450m above town) for panoramic views of the Remarkables and Lake Wakatipu. Walk the Tiki Trail back down through native bush (~1.5 hours, moderate).
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit Queenstown Gardens for a relaxed walk among century-old trees and rose gardens on the lake peninsula. Head to Arrowtown (~25 min drive) — a beautifully preserved 1860s gold-rush village. Walk the Arrow River trail and visit the Chinese Settlement historic site.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown. Browse the night markets (if Monday market is running seasonally) or enjoy the lakefront atmosphere.

meals.breakfast: Vudu Café & Larder on Rees Street — excellent eggs, avocado toast, and flat whites. ~NZD 18–25.
meals.lunch: Arrowtown's Provisions café — fresh sandwiches, cabinet food, and great coffee in a charming heritage setting. ~NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: The Cow Restaurant, Queenstown — cozy stone-walled restaurant famous for pizza and pasta. Great mid-range option. ~NZD 25–35.

day_by_day.notes: Wear comfortable walking shoes for Tiki Trail — it's steep in places. Arrowtown is a highlight not to rush. November daylight extends to ~9:30 PM in Queenstown, giving you long evenings to enjoy.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Nevis Bungy Jump: Transfer to the Nevis Bungy platform (~30 min from Queenstown via 4WD shuttle). Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. The 8.5-second free fall is an iconic adrenaline experience. Morning slots are recommended before wind picks up.
day_by_day.afternoon: Recovery and debrief! Head back to Queenstown and treat yourself to a relaxed afternoon. Visit the Queenstown waterfront, rent a paddleboard or kayak on Lake Wakatipu for a gentle contrast to the morning's adrenaline.
day_by_day.evening: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk: Join the guided evening walk through Queenstown's town center and lakefront, sampling local cuisine and learning about Māori culture and the town's gold-rush heritage. ~2.5 hours.

meals.breakfast: Early, light breakfast at the hotel before the bungy transfer — banana, toast, and coffee. Avoid heavy meals before jumping.
meals.lunch: Bao Now food truck or Queenstown's food precinct — Asian-inspired bao buns and noodles, quick and satisfying post-jump fuel. ~NZD 15–18.
meals.dinner: Included tastings during the Night Food Walk. Supplement with a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir at a local wine bar afterward — try Atlas Beer Café.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Nevis Bungy well in advance — it sells out fast, especially in summer (November). Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes with no loose items. Weight limit applies (45–127 kg). The food walk typically departs around 6:00–6:30 PM — confirm exact time at booking. Minimum age 13 for bungy.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Glenorchy (~45 min from Queenstown along a stunning lake road). Walk the Glenorchy Lagoon Boardwalk and explore the historic town. Continue to Paradise — a remote valley used as a filming location for Lord of the Rings.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Rob Roy Glacier Track from Wanaka direction OR take the shorter Mount Alfred Track above Glenorchy (2–3 hours return, moderate, panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu and surrounding peaks). Return to Queenstown via the scenic lake road.
day_by_day.evening: Relax at the hotel. Enjoy the Nevis Valley surroundings at dusk — look for native birds including kea (alpine parrots) in the area.

meals.breakfast: Hotel breakfast or self-catered at accommodation. Pack snacks and lunch for the day's hiking.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch from a Queenstown supermarket (New World or Countdown) — sandwiches, fruit, trail mix. Eat at a scenic Glenorchy picnic spot by the lake.
meals.dinner: Vudu Larder & Café (evening menu) or Rata Restaurant — chef-driven New Zealand cuisine using local South Island produce. ~NZD 35–50 per person.

day_by_day.notes: The Queenstown–Glenorchy road is one of the most scenic drives in New Zealand — take your time. Fill up on petrol in Queenstown before heading out. The Paradise road may require a high-clearance vehicle depending on conditions — check locally. Bring layers; mountain weather can change quickly.

day_by_day.morning: Drive to Te Anau (~2 hours from Queenstown). Stop at Kingston and Five Rivers for views. Arrive in Te Anau — the gateway to Fiordland. Check in to mid-range accommodation (pre-booked). Explore the Te Anau lakefront and town.
day_by_day.afternoon: Te Anau Glowworm Caves boat tour — cruise across Lake Te Anau and explore the underground cave system lit by thousands of glowworms. A magical and unique Fiordland experience (~2.5 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Stroll along the Te Anau lakefront at sunset. The Kepler Mountains reflect beautifully in the lake in calm conditions.

meals.breakfast: Hotel or café breakfast before departure — Miles Better Pies in Queenstown for a savory pie on the road. ~NZD 8–12.
meals.lunch: The Sandfly Café in Te Anau — cozy, good value, excellent cabinet food and hot meals. ~NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: The Fat Duck, Te Anau — popular local restaurant with New Zealand lamb, venison, and fresh fish. Great mid-range option. ~NZD 30–45.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour in advance through Real Journeys — it's very popular in November. The caves are cool inside (~12°C) so bring a light jacket. Te Anau is a small town — most services are on the main street. This is your base for the Milford Sound experience tomorrow.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo: Depart Te Anau early (typically 6:00–7:00 AM transfer). Drive the spectacular Milford Road through Homer Tunnel. Arrive at Milford Sound and begin the dawn kayak through the fiord — paddle beneath Mitre Peak and Stirling Falls before cruise ships arrive. Absolutely magical in early morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue with the hike component of the combo — walk the Milford foreshore and surrounding trails with your guide. Spot fur seals, dolphins (if lucky), and waterfalls cascading down sheer granite walls. Return transfer to Te Anau in the afternoon.
day_by_day.evening: Arrive back in Te Anau early evening. Quiet recovery dinner and early night — legs will be tired!

meals.breakfast: Very early — eat at the hotel before 6:00 AM departure. Pack energy bars and snacks for the kayak.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch provided by the tour operator or eat at the Milford Sound Lodge café upon return from kayaking. ~NZD 15–20.
meals.dinner: Redcliff Restaurant, Te Anau — set in a charming old cottage, serving excellent Fiordland venison and local seafood. ~NZD 35–50.

day_by_day.notes: This is a full, physically demanding day — wear warm, moisture-wicking layers under your wetsuit (provided). Sandflies at Milford Sound are notoriously aggressive — bring strong insect repellent. Waterproof bags are provided for cameras. November weather at Milford can be unpredictable — the fiord is stunning in both sun and rain (rain creates hundreds of temporary waterfalls). Confirm exact pickup time with operator.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Routeburn Track Great Walk (Day 1 of 2): Drive from Te Anau to the Routeburn Shelter trailhead (~1.5 hours via Glenorchy). Begin the iconic 32km Routeburn Track. Hike from the Routeburn Shelter through ancient beech forest to Routeburn Flats Hut (11.4km, ~3–4 hours, easy-moderate). Stunning river valley scenery.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue from Routeburn Flats to Routeburn Falls Hut (2.3km, ~1 hour, steep climb). Arrive at the hut perched above the treeline with spectacular alpine views. Explore the area around the hut and the dramatic Routeburn Falls.
day_by_day.evening: Settle into Routeburn Falls Hut (DOC Great Walk hut, pre-booked). Cook dinner in the communal hut kitchen, meet fellow trampers from around the world. Enjoy the alpine twilight from the hut deck.

meals.breakfast: Early hotel breakfast in Te Anau before departure.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch — crackers, cheese, salami, dried fruit, chocolate. Eat at Routeburn Flats.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked hut meal — pre-packed dehydrated meal (Mountain House or Back Country Cuisine) plus hot drinks. Available from outdoor stores in Queenstown or Te Anau.

day_by_day.notes: DOC Great Walk hut passes MUST be booked in advance — Routeburn Track is one of the most popular Great Walks and November (peak season) books out months ahead. Book at doc.govt.nz. Pack all food, a sleeping bag liner, and personal items. Hut provides mattresses, toilets, and cooking facilities. Weight your pack carefully — aim for under 12kg. Trekking poles recommended for the steep section to Falls Hut.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk (Day 2 of 2): Rise early and hike from Routeburn Falls Hut over the Harris Saddle (the high point at 1,255m — incredible panoramic views of Fiordland and Mount Aspiring NP). Continue to Lake Mackenzie Hut (11.4km from Falls Hut, ~4–5 hours). This is the most dramatic and rewarding section of the track.
day_by_day.afternoon: Swim in Lake Mackenzie (cold but exhilarating!), rest, and enjoy the stunning glacial lake surrounded by peaks. Optional: hike the Emily Peak side trip from the saddle for even more dramatic views (+2 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Lake Mackenzie Hut. Socialize with fellow trampers. Watch the alpenglow on the surrounding peaks at sunset — one of the most beautiful evenings imaginable.

meals.breakfast: Porridge, muesli, or instant oats cooked at the hut. Coffee or tea.
meals.lunch: Trail snacks and packed lunch eaten at Harris Saddle — the views make it unforgettable.
meals.dinner: Dehydrated hut meal — try a curry or pasta option. Hot chocolate for dessert.

day_by_day.notes: Harris Saddle can be exposed and windy — pack a waterproof shell and warm mid-layer regardless of forecast. The saddle section can be snow-covered in early November but should be clear by late November — check DOC conditions report before departure. This is the highlight of the entire track for most hikers.

day_by_day.morning: Routeburn Track Great Walk (Day 3 — final section): Hike from Lake Mackenzie Hut to The Divide (8.3km, ~3 hours, mostly downhill through stunning beech forest). Pass the Earland Falls (174m waterfall) — a spectacular highlight. Arrive at The Divide car park.
day_by_day.afternoon: Pre-arranged shuttle or bus from The Divide back to Te Anau or Queenstown (~2 hours). Shower, rest, and recover. If returning to Queenstown, check back into Nevis Valley accommodation.
day_by_day.evening: Celebratory dinner in Queenstown to mark completing the Routeburn Track. You've earned it!

meals.breakfast: Final hut breakfast — use up remaining trail food.
meals.lunch: Packed trail lunch on the final section, or eat at Te Anau on the return journey.
meals.dinner: Botswana Butchery, Queenstown — lakeside fine-casual dining, excellent New Zealand beef and lamb. Celebrate the Great Walk completion. ~NZD 45–65 per person.

day_by_day.notes: Book the Routeburn Track shuttle (Tracknet or similar) in advance — The Divide is remote and there's no public transport. The shuttle typically connects with buses back to Queenstown via Te Anau. Legs will be sore — pack ibuprofen and blister plasters. Do laundry tonight in preparation for the remaining days.

day_by_day.morning: Active rest day in Queenstown. Sleep in and enjoy a slow morning. Visit the Queenstown Farmers Market (Saturday market — check if a weekday version runs) or browse local galleries and craft shops. Light stretching or yoga to recover from the Routeburn.
day_by_day.afternoon: Drive to Wanaka (~1 hour over Crown Range — the highest sealed road in NZ, stunning views). Visit the iconic 'That Wanaka Tree' on the lake shore. Walk the Wanaka lakefront and explore the charming town center. Visit Puzzling World for a fun, quirky attraction.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown via the Crown Range at sunset — extraordinary golden-hour views over Central Otago. Or stay in Wanaka for dinner and return after.

meals.breakfast: Bespoke Kitchen, Queenstown — one of the best brunch spots in town. Excellent eggs, smoothie bowls, and specialty coffee. ~NZD 20–28.
meals.lunch: Francesca's Italian Kitchen, Wanaka — authentic Italian pasta and pizza in a relaxed setting. ~NZD 22–30.
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro (between Queenstown and Wanaka) — stunning vineyard setting, excellent Central Otago Pinot Noir, and seasonal tasting menu. ~NZD 50–70. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Crown Range road is spectacular but can be narrow and winding — drive carefully, especially at dusk. Wanaka is increasingly popular and has a more relaxed vibe than Queenstown — many visitors prefer it. November is a beautiful time in Central Otago with wildflowers and long days.

day_by_day.morning: FEATURED EXPERIENCE — Mueller Hut Route, Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (Day 1): Drive from Queenstown to Mount Cook Village (~2.5 hours via Lake Pukaki — the vivid turquoise glacial lake is breathtaking). Begin the Mueller Hut Route — a challenging 10km return hike gaining 1,030m elevation. Start early (by 9:00 AM). Hike through the Sealy Tarns to Mueller Hut perched dramatically above the Hooker Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Mueller Hut (2,015m elevation) with jaw-dropping views of Aoraki/Mount Cook (3,724m — NZ's highest peak), the Mueller and Hooker Glaciers, and surrounding Southern Alps. Explore the area around the hut. Spot kea alpine parrots.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight at Mueller Hut (pre-booked DOC hut, 28 bunks). Watch the sunset paint Aoraki gold and orange — one of the most spectacular sights in New Zealand. Stargazing from the hut deck in the Aoraki Mackenzie Dark Sky Reserve — exceptional.

meals.breakfast: Early breakfast at hotel before departure. Pack substantial trail snacks for the climb.
meals.lunch: Packed lunch eaten at Sealy Tarns or Mueller Hut — the views make every bite better.
meals.dinner: Self-cooked dehydrated meal at the hut. Hot drinks. Bring extra snacks — the altitude and cold increase appetite.

day_by_day.notes: Mueller Hut is one of the most spectacular hut experiences in New Zealand — book months in advance at doc.govt.nz. The track involves a steep staircase section (2,200 steps) and exposed alpine terrain. Weather at Mount Cook changes rapidly — check MetService forecast and DOC conditions before departure. Bring a warm sleeping bag (temperatures can drop below freezing at night even in November), headlamp, and full rain gear. The Lake Pukaki viewpoint en route is unmissable — allow 20 minutes to stop.

day_by_day.morning: Wake before sunrise at Mueller Hut for the golden-hour view of Aoraki — absolutely unforgettable. Descend the Mueller Hut Route back to Mount Cook Village (~2–3 hours). Visit the Sir Edmund Hillary Alpine Centre at The Hermitage hotel — excellent museum about NZ mountaineering history.
day_by_day.afternoon: Hike the Hooker Valley Track (10km return, easy, flat) — one of the most rewarding easy walks in NZ, passing three swing bridges with direct views of Aoraki and the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with floating icebergs. Return to Queenstown via Lake Pukaki and Lindis Pass (~3 hours).
day_by_day.evening: Final evening in Queenstown. Relax and reflect on an extraordinary two weeks in the South Island.

meals.breakfast: Sunrise breakfast at Mueller Hut — porridge and coffee with the best view in New Zealand.
meals.lunch: Old Mountaineers' Café, Mount Cook Village — great burgers, pies, and coffee in a characterful setting. ~NZD 18–25.
meals.dinner: Queenstown farewell dinner — Rata Restaurant by Josh Emett, featuring the best of New Zealand's seasonal produce and Central Otago wines. ~NZD 50–70. Reserve in advance.

day_by_day.notes: The Hooker Valley Track is deceptively beautiful for such an easy walk — don't skip it thinking it's too simple. The icebergs in the terminal lake are a surreal sight. The drive back via Lindis Pass and Cromwell offers stunning tawny Central Otago hill country. Fill up with petrol at Twizel on the return journey.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning in Queenstown. Slow breakfast and pack. Take one last walk along the Lake Wakatipu waterfront and up to the Queenstown Hill Time Walk (1.5 hours return, moderate) for a final panoramic farewell view over the town, lake, and Remarkables.
day_by_day.afternoon: Check out of Nevis Valley accommodation. Browse Queenstown's boutique shops for souvenirs — look for locally made pounamu (greenstone) jewelry, Merino wool products, and Central Otago wine to take home. Transfer to Queenstown Airport for departure.
day_by_day.evening: Departure from Queenstown Airport. Carry memories of an extraordinary South Island adventure — bungy jumping, Great Walks, fiords, glaciers, and some of the most dramatic landscapes on Earth.

meals.breakfast: Final New Zealand breakfast at Vudu Café — eggs benedict, flat white, and fresh-squeezed juice. ~NZD 22–28.
meals.lunch: Queenstown airport café or a final Fergburger if time allows before departure.
meals.dinner: In-flight meal or at destination airport.

day_by_day.notes: Allow at least 2 hours before departure for Queenstown Airport check-in — international connections may require more. Declare any food items at customs. New Zealand has strict biosecurity rules — do not attempt to bring fresh food, soil, or plant material through customs. Consider purchasing travel insurance claim receipts for any gear or activity-related expenses. The South Island is extraordinary — start planning your return!

highlights: Mix of paid and free experiences

trip_options.title: Premium New Zealand South Island Escape
trip_options.description: Indulge in the best the destination has to offer. Premium flights, luxury hotels, and exclusive experiences.

experiences.name: Nevis Bungy Jump
experiences.description: Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform at 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. This iconic AJ Hackett experience offers a 8.5-second freefall with breathtaking views of the surrounding Remarkables mountain range. Includes transport from Queenstown and a commemorative video package.

experiences.name: Routeburn Track Great Walk
experiences.description: Hike one of New Zealand's nine Great Walks, a stunning 32km trail through Fiordland and Mount Aspiring National Parks. Trek through ancient beech forests, alpine meadows, and past glacial lakes with panoramic views of the Harris Saddle. Can be done as a guided day section or multi-day trek with DOC huts.

experiences.name: Tongariro Alpine Crossing — South Island Alternative: Mueller Hut Route
experiences.description: Tackle the challenging Mueller Hut Route in Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park, a 10km return hike gaining 1000m elevation. Reward yourself with jaw-dropping views of the Hooker Valley, Mueller Glacier, and the Southern Alps. Overnight stays in the DOC Mueller Hut offer unforgettable stargazing in one of the world's darkest sky reserves.

experiences.name: Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo
experiences.description: Paddle through the dramatic fiords of Milford Sound at dawn before the cruise ships arrive, gliding past Mitre Peak and cascading waterfalls. Combine with a guided walk along the Milford foreshore track through ancient rainforest. A truly immersive way to experience one of the world's most spectacular natural wonders.

experiences.name: Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk
experiences.description: Explore Queenstown's vibrant culinary scene on a guided evening walk through the town center and lakefront. Sample locally sourced Central Otago pinot noir, artisan cheeses, venison sliders, and Fergburger — the legendary burger institution. Learn about Māori culture and the region's gold rush history from knowledgeable local guides.

day_by_day.morning: Arrival at Queenstown Airport at 13:00 — no morning activities scheduled. Rest and prepare for transfer.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer from Queenstown Airport to Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Check in, settle into your premium accommodation, and enjoy a welcome orientation with your host. Take a leisurely stroll around the property and soak in the dramatic Nevis Valley landscape.
day_by_day.evening: Relax on the property terrace with a curated welcome drink and charcuterie board prepared by the in-house chef. Enjoy a private sunset viewing over the Nevis gorge — one of the most spectacular vistas in Central Otago.

meals.breakfast: Not applicable — mid-day arrival
meals.lunch: Light premium grazing board and sparkling wine provided upon check-in at the boutique stay
meals.dinner: Private in-house chef dinner at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — expect Central Otago lamb, locally sourced seasonal vegetables, and a curated Central Otago Pinot Noir wine pairing

day_by_day.notes: Flight LH lands at 13:00. Allow approximately 45–60 minutes for customs, baggage collection, and meeting your private transfer driver. No strenuous activities are planned today to allow for jet lag recovery. Confirm any dietary requirements with the property in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Fuel up with a gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay before heading out for a private guided exploration of the Nevis Valley highland terrain. Walk along the historic Nevis Road and take in the gold-rush era schist rock formations, tussock grasslands, and panoramic views of the Remarkables mountain range.
day_by_day.afternoon: Experience the crown jewel of your trip — the Nevis Bungy Jump. Leap from New Zealand's highest bungy platform, 134 meters above the Nevis River gorge. A private shuttle will take you to the Nevis Bungy complex from Queenstown's base. Your premium package includes a private pre-jump briefing, GoPro footage package, and a commemorative certificate.
day_by_day.evening: Return to Queenstown township for the Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk — a guided evening stroll through the town center and lakefront, sampling premium New Zealand cuisine, craft beverages, and local artisan produce at curated stops.

meals.breakfast: Full gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — eggs benedict with smoked salmon, fresh fruit platters, and French press single-origin coffee
meals.lunch: Premium picnic hamper provided by the boutique stay, enjoyed at a scenic Nevis Valley viewpoint before heading to the bungy
meals.dinner: Multi-stop premium dining experience as part of the Queenstown Night Food and Culture Walk — includes fine canapés, Central Otago wine tastings, and artisan cheese boards

day_by_day.notes: The Nevis Bungy requires a minimum weight of 45kg and maximum of 127kg. Wear comfortable, close-toed shoes. The experience includes a gondola-style cable car to the platform over the gorge. Book the food walk in advance to secure a small private group experience.

day_by_day.morning: Recovery morning — enjoy a slow, indulgent breakfast at the boutique stay followed by a private yoga or stretching session on the terrace (arrange with the property in advance). Spend time journaling or reading with views of the Nevis Valley.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private helicopter tour departing from Queenstown over the Southern Alps, Remarkables, and Lake Wakatipu. Land on a remote alpine snowfield for a champagne toast before returning. This bespoke experience offers unmatched aerial perspectives of the South Island's dramatic interior.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Queenstown's finest restaurant — Amisfield Winery & Bistro in the Gibbston Valley, just a short drive from the property. Enjoy a degustation menu featuring estate-grown produce paired with Amisfield's award-winning Pinot Noir and Pinot Gris in an elegant cellar-door setting.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — house-made granola, stone fruit compote, freshly baked sourdough, and cold-pressed juices
meals.lunch: Light alpine charcuterie and sparkling wine served during the helicopter snowfield landing
meals.dinner: Amisfield Winery & Bistro degustation menu — 6 courses with full wine pairing, approximately NZD $250–$350 per person

day_by_day.notes: Helicopter tours are weather-dependent. Have a backup activity arranged (e.g., private wine tour of Gibbston Valley cellars) in case of adverse conditions. Amisfield reservations should be made weeks in advance.

day_by_day.morning: Early departure by private vehicle toward the Routeburn Track trailhead (approximately 1.5 hours from Queenstown via Glenorchy). Begin the first section of the Routeburn Track Great Walk — hike from the Routeburn Shelter through ancient beech forests to Routeburn Flats, approximately 2.5 hours of moderate hiking with stunning river and mountain views.
day_by_day.afternoon: Continue the trail from Routeburn Flats up to Routeburn Falls Hut, gaining dramatic altitude with cascading waterfalls and alpine meadows unfolding around you. Enjoy a premium packed lunch at the falls viewpoint. This section takes approximately 2–3 hours and is one of the most scenic on the entire track.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the trailhead via private guide and transfer back to the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Enjoy a warm soak in the property's private outdoor bath or hot tub before a restorative dinner.

meals.breakfast: Early high-protein gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — smashed avocado on sourdough, poached eggs, smoked salmon, and a thermos of premium coffee for the road
meals.lunch: Premium hiker's hamper prepared by the boutique stay — artisan sandwiches, local cheeses, bliss balls, fruit, and electrolyte drinks enjoyed at Routeburn Falls
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the boutique stay — pan-seared South Island salmon, roasted root vegetables, and a Central Otago Riesling

day_by_day.notes: The Routeburn Track is a multi-day Great Walk, but this itinerary covers the most spectacular day-hike sections (Routeburn Shelter to Routeburn Falls, return). Wear layered clothing as alpine weather can change rapidly in November. Hire a private licensed guide for the best interpretation of the flora, fauna, and geology.

day_by_day.morning: Leisure morning at the boutique stay. Enjoy a late breakfast and explore the immediate surrounds of the Nevis Valley on a self-guided walk along the property trails. Take time to photograph the dramatic schist landscape and tussock-covered hills in the morning light.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private transfer to Arrowtown — a beautifully preserved gold-rush village 20 minutes from Queenstown. Explore the heritage Chinese settlement, browse boutique galleries and antique shops, and visit the Lakes District Museum for a curated introduction to the region's history.
day_by_day.evening: Dinner at Provisions of Arrowtown or The Chop Shop — both offering premium farm-to-table dining in a charming gold-rush ambiance. Enjoy locally sourced venison, lamb, and seasonal produce with an extensive New Zealand wine list.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely late breakfast at the boutique stay — Belgian waffles with seasonal berries, whipped cream, and maple syrup
meals.lunch: Artisan lunch at a curated Arrowtown café — gourmet pies, local cheeses, and a glass of Central Otago Pinot Noir
meals.dinner: Provisions of Arrowtown — seasonal degustation with local wine pairing, approximately NZD $180–$250 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrowtown is particularly beautiful in November when the willows and poplars along Arrow River are in full leaf. Consider a short walk along the Arrow River before dinner.

day_by_day.morning: Private 4WD adventure tour through the Nevis Valley and surrounding high country stations. Your expert guide will take you deep into the backcountry, visiting historic gold-dredging sites, crossing remote riverbeds, and accessing viewpoints unreachable by standard vehicles.
day_by_day.afternoon: Visit a working high-country merino sheep station for a private farm experience — watch a sheepdog demonstration, learn about merino wool farming, and enjoy a homestead afternoon tea with scones, jam, and cream.
day_by_day.evening: Return to the boutique stay for a private stargazing experience. The Nevis Valley's extreme remoteness and low light pollution make it one of the South Island's premier dark sky locations. A telescope and astronomy guide will be arranged for a guided celestial tour.

meals.breakfast: Gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — eggs any style, house-cured bacon, grilled tomatoes, and freshly squeezed orange juice
meals.lunch: Homestead afternoon tea at the high-country station — freshly baked scones, local honey, clotted cream, and a selection of herbal teas
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the boutique stay — slow-braised high-country venison with red wine reduction, roasted kumara, and wilted greens

day_by_day.notes: Dress warmly for the evening stargazing session — even in November, Nevis Valley nights can be cool. The 4WD tour requires sturdy footwear. Confirm the high-country station visit is pre-arranged through your concierge.

day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer toward Aoraki/Mount Cook National Park (approximately 3.5–4 hours from Queenstown via the Mackenzie Basin). En route, stop at Lake Pukaki for photographs of the impossibly turquoise glacial waters with Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected on the surface.
day_by_day.afternoon: Begin the Mueller Hut Route — one of the South Island's most dramatic alpine day hikes. The 10km return trail gains significant elevation through the Sealy Tarns to Mueller Hut, rewarding you with jaw-dropping views of the Hooker Valley, Mueller Glacier, and Aoraki/Mount Cook. Allow 5–7 hours for the full return journey.
day_by_day.evening: Descend and transfer to The Hermitage Hotel — Mount Cook's iconic luxury lodge. Check in and enjoy a premium dinner at The Panorama Restaurant with floor-to-ceiling views of the Southern Alps.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box prepared by the boutique stay for an early departure — fresh fruit, muffins, hard-boiled eggs, and a thermos of coffee
meals.lunch: Premium alpine lunch pack enjoyed at Mueller Hut — energy-rich wraps, trail mix, chocolate, and hydration drinks
meals.dinner: The Panorama Restaurant at The Hermitage Hotel — à la carte fine dining with South Island lamb, local salmon, and New Zealand wine list. Approximately NZD $120–$180 per person

day_by_day.notes: The Mueller Hut Route is a challenging Grade 3 alpine hike with significant elevation gain (approximately 1,000 meters). Trekking poles are strongly recommended. Book a licensed alpine guide for safety and enhanced experience. Overnight at The Hermitage Hotel for this night — a change from the Nevis Valley base.

day_by_day.morning: Sunrise walk along the Hooker Valley Track from The Hermitage — a relatively flat 10km return trail leading to the Hooker Glacier terminal lake with stunning views of Aoraki/Mount Cook reflected in the glacial waters. One of the most accessible yet breathtaking walks in New Zealand.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private scenic flight over Aoraki/Mount Cook, the Tasman Glacier, and the Southern Alps — including a glacier landing on the Tasman Glacier snowfield. This is a once-in-a-lifetime aerial perspective of New Zealand's highest peaks.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay (approximately 4 hours). Enjoy a relaxed evening with a private chef dinner and wine tasting on the property.

meals.breakfast: Full buffet breakfast at The Hermitage Hotel before the morning walk
meals.lunch: Light lunch at The Old Mountaineers' Café in Mount Cook Village — gourmet sandwiches and locally made pies
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — house-made pasta with Central Otago truffle oil, aged parmesan, and a premium Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc

day_by_day.notes: The Tasman Glacier scenic flight is weather-dependent — have a backup afternoon planned (e.g., guided glacier walk or Tasman Lake kayak). The return drive to Queenstown is long — consider an audioguide or curated playlist of New Zealand music for the journey.

day_by_day.morning: Rest and recovery day at the boutique stay. Enjoy a luxurious slow morning — in-room spa treatments can be arranged through the property (massage, facial, or hydrotherapy). Spend time reading on the terrace with views over the Nevis gorge.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private wine tour of the Gibbston Valley — known as the 'Valley of the Vines,' this stunning gorge is home to some of New Zealand's finest Pinot Noir producers. Visit 3–4 premium cellar doors including Peregrine Wines, Carrick Winery, and Gibbston Valley Wines with a private sommelier guide.
day_by_day.evening: Sunset dinner at Kinross Gibbston — a premium winery restaurant set in a dramatic schist stone building in the Gibbston Valley, offering farm-to-table cuisine and an exceptional wine list.

meals.breakfast: Leisurely gourmet breakfast at the boutique stay — house-made granola parfait, smashed avocado, and a full barista coffee service
meals.lunch: Premium cheese and charcuterie tasting boards at Gibbston Valley Wines cellar door, paired with their flagship Pinot Noir
meals.dinner: Kinross Gibbston — seasonal à la carte menu with Central Otago wine pairing. Approximately NZD $150–$200 per person

day_by_day.notes: Arrange a dedicated driver for the wine tour — do not self-drive after tastings. Most cellar doors in Gibbston Valley are open from 10am–5pm. Pre-book private tastings for the best experience.

day_by_day.morning: Early private transfer to Te Anau (approximately 2 hours from Queenstown). Check in to a premium lakeside lodge. Begin the journey toward Milford Sound via the iconic Milford Road — stopping at Mirror Lakes, The Chasm, and Homer Tunnel for photographs and short walks.
day_by_day.afternoon: Arrive at Milford Sound for the Milford Sound Kayak and Hike Combo — paddle through the dramatic fiords in a private guided kayak session, gliding beneath Mitre Peak and past thundering waterfalls. Follow with a guided shoreline walk through ancient rainforest.
day_by_day.evening: Overnight cruise on Milford Sound aboard a premium small-vessel overnight cruise — enjoy a gourmet dinner, wildlife spotting (dolphins, seals, penguins), and wake up inside the fiord at dawn.

meals.breakfast: Packed gourmet breakfast box for the road — pastries, fruit, and coffee from a premium Te Anau café
meals.lunch: Premium packed lunch enjoyed on the kayak or at a scenic fiord-side stop — artisan wraps, energy bars, and fresh fruit
meals.dinner: Gourmet dinner aboard the Milford Sound overnight cruise — fresh seafood, South Island lamb, and New Zealand wines served in a panoramic dining saloon

day_by_day.notes: The Milford Road is one of the world's great scenic drives — allow extra time for stops. The overnight Milford Sound cruise is one of New Zealand's most exclusive experiences — book months in advance. Bring waterproof layers for kayaking.

day_by_day.morning: Wake up inside Milford Sound at dawn — one of the most magical experiences in New Zealand. Watch the first light illuminate Mitre Peak and the surrounding fiord walls from the deck of your cruise vessel. A continental breakfast is served on board.
day_by_day.afternoon: Disembark and return via the Milford Road to Te Anau. Stop at the Te Anau Glowworm Caves for a private guided boat tour through an ancient underground limestone cave system illuminated by thousands of glowworms.
day_by_day.evening: Return transfer to the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay (approximately 2 hours from Te Anau). Enjoy a quiet, restorative evening with a private chef dinner and reflection on the fiordland experience.

meals.breakfast: Continental breakfast aboard the Milford Sound cruise vessel — pastries, fresh fruit, yogurt, and coffee
meals.lunch: Premium lunch at a Te Anau lakeside restaurant — pan-seared blue cod, local greens, and a glass of Marlborough Sauvignon Blanc
meals.dinner: Private chef dinner at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — slow-cooked lamb shoulder, roasted vegetables, and a final Central Otago Pinot Noir from the property's curated cellar

day_by_day.notes: The Te Anau Glowworm Caves tour requires advance booking and is run by Real Journeys. The caves are a UNESCO World Heritage-listed environment — photography with flash is not permitted inside.

day_by_day.morning: Final full-day adventure — return to Queenstown for a private jet boat experience on the Shotover River, followed by a scenic gondola ride to the Skyline complex for panoramic views over Lake Wakatipu and the Remarkables.
day_by_day.afternoon: Luxury shopping and exploration in Queenstown's premium boutiques — browse New Zealand merino wool garments, pounamu (greenstone) jewelry, and artisan souvenirs. Visit a premium chocolatier and local food producers for gifts.
day_by_day.evening: Farewell dinner at Queenstown's most celebrated fine dining venue — Rata Restaurant by Josh Emett. Enjoy a beautifully crafted seasonal menu celebrating New Zealand's finest produce, with an extensive wine list and impeccable service.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet breakfast at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay — a special send-off spread with all your favorites from the week
meals.lunch: Light premium lunch at Skyline Queenstown's Stratosfare Restaurant — buffet with panoramic views of Lake Wakatipu
meals.dinner: Rata Restaurant by Josh Emett — 5-course tasting menu with wine pairing. Approximately NZD $200–$280 per person. Reservations essential.

day_by_day.notes: Pack your luggage and leave it at the boutique stay for collection — check-out procedures should be confirmed with the property the evening before. The jet boat experience is a classic Queenstown adventure and suitable for all fitness levels.

day_by_day.morning: Final morning at the Nevis Valley Boutique Stay. Enjoy a leisurely farewell breakfast and take one last walk around the property to absorb the stunning landscape. Exchange contact details with your host and collect any final recommendations.
day_by_day.afternoon: Private luxury transfer to Queenstown Airport for your departure flight. Allow at least 2 hours before departure for check-in and security. Reflect on 13 extraordinary days across the South Island.
day_by_day.evening: Departure — carry with you memories of the world's highest bungy, the Routeburn Track, Milford Sound at dawn, Mueller Hut's alpine grandeur, and the incomparable hospitality of the Nevis Valley.

meals.breakfast: Final gourmet farewell breakfast at the boutique stay — your choice from the week's favorites, with a special house-made gift hamper of Central Otago preserves and wines to take home
meals.lunch: Premium airport lounge dining at Queenstown Airport or a final café stop in Queenstown township before transfer
meals.dinner: In-flight or at your onward destination

day_by_day.notes: Queenstown Airport has a well-appointed Air New Zealand Koru Lounge — confirm lounge access with your airline or travel agent. Ensure all purchased goods comply with your home country's customs regulations, particularly any food items from the gift hamper. Allow extra baggage weight for souvenirs and merino purchases.
